_what: O-UNGRADED-MECHANISM-CLAIMS. Every sentence in this repository that describes how a mechanism works in the shapes below is a CANDIDATE. Each candidate is judged here (`claims`) or counted in `backlog`. Read by tooling/ci/assert-mechanism-claims.mjs, and by nothing else.
_rule: A NEW candidate arrives with a `claims` entry, or the build is red. `proven`: `test` + `case` name a test that fails when the sentence goes false, and `proves` says how. `demoted`: `reason` says why the sentence asserts nothing a test could grade. An entry covers the candidates that start on a line inside its `anchor`, which must appear exactly once in `file`. `backlog` is the count of unjudged candidates per file, measured when the guard landed. It may only shrink: judge a site, or reword it, and lower the row in the same change. `node tooling/ci/assert-mechanism-claims.mjs --measure` prints the rows the tree implies.
_shapes: A single space in `pattern` stands for whitespace and comment leaders, so a sentence that wraps across comment lines still matches. Case-insensitive. The shapes only FIND candidates; whether a sentence is true is a reader's judgement, recorded below (trap grep-02).

shapes.why: The seed sentence (verify-supabase-templates.mjs) said there was no second list, over a loop that walked one.
Says a mechanism maintains itself. False the day somebody adds the list it says is not needed.
Says two things are held together by construction. True only while the construction under it is what the sentence says.
The same promise as cannot-drift, in other words.
The seed defect's own wording, next to code that derived nothing.
Says a set is computed from its source. A hardcoded set under the same sentence reads identically.
